Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Vitalis Medical Devices, Inc. Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Michael Reynolds, CEO; Lisa Chen, CFO; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and Tom Hargrove, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Vitalis Medical Devices delivered strong results this quarter, driven by increasing adoption of our innovative medical devices and strategic partnerships.

Today, I will cover five key aspects of our performance: our overall performance highlights and key achievements; organic revenue growth by segment and geography; procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary; capital equipment versus consumables mix trends; and R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress.

Lisa will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. After that, we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with our overall performance highlights and key achievements. I'm thrilled to kick off with these, as they underscore another quarter of robust execution in a dynamic medtech landscape. Our diversified portfolio—spanning cardiovascular interventions, orthopedic implants, neuromodulation therapies, and fast-growing robotics and digital health platforms—is capitalizing on secular tailwinds like the aging global population, value-based care shifts, and minimally invasive procedure adoption.

Top-line, we reported net revenue of $1.28 billion, up 14% year-over-year reported and 15% organically, beating our guidance midpoint and consensus. This is our eighth straight quarter of double-digit organic growth, fueled by volume, pricing discipline, and procedural gains across core franchises. Constant currency growth hit 16%, thanks to proactive hedging against European FX volatility.

Bottom-line strength showed in adjusted diluted EPS of $1.62, up 17%, with operating margins expanding 250 basis points to 28.4%. GAAP EPS was $1.41, reflecting non-cash amortization from our NeuroStim Dynamics acquisition. Free cash flow reached $450 million, up 22% year-over-year, supporting $300 million in share repurchases under our $2 billion program and our 12th consecutive quarterly dividend increase to $0.45 per share.

In cardiovascular, 42% of revenue, we grew 18% organically to $535 million. Our VitalFlow DES platform grabbed 2.2 incremental share points in the U.S. coronary market to 28%, per Millennium Research, while VitalClip transcatheter mitral repair exceeded 15,000 global implants since FDA approval, with volumes up 45% year-over-year, rivaling Abbott's MitraClip.

Orthopedics, 25% of revenue, advanced 12% organically to $320 million, powered by Mako robotic-arm systems hitting over 50,000 procedures this quarter and a 15% attach rate for cementless Triad implants. Revision rates dropped 8% in our base, affirming durable solutions amid readmission scrutiny.

Neuromodulation and robotics surged 28% organically to $285 million, 22% of revenue. NeuroVibe spinal cord stimulator, post-PMA approval, generated $45 million in early sales, cutting opioid use 30% versus legacy systems like Medtronic's Intellis, aligning with CMS mandates. VitalBot surgical robot utilization hit 85% via Siemens Healthineers imaging partnerships, at 25% lower cost-per-procedure than Intuitive Surgical.

Regionally, U.S. grew 17% organically, aided by 2024 IPPS reimbursement boosts for robotic ortho. Europe expanded 11% despite German budget softness, with VitalFlow stents gaining in UK and France PCI volumes up 9% per EuroPCR. Asia-Pacific jumped 25%, China leading via Mindray JDA for ortho implants; emerging markets like India and Brazil added $120 million, up 35%, with EssentialCare portfolio.

Key achievements include pipeline acceleration with six new 510(k)s and PMAs, like CardioSense AI monitor for AFib in the $15 billion digital therapeutics space growing 22% CAGR. R&D hit 12.5% of revenue at $160 million, 45% to AI/ML. The $1.2 billion NeuroStim deal yields $50 million run-rate synergies, cross-selling into our 2 million CRM patients; plus a Philips JV for hybrid ORs targeting $8 billion market.

Sustainability-wise, dual-sourced nitinol ensured 99.8% delivery amid Red Sea issues; Scope 3 emissions down 25% with recycled titanium, landing us on Newsweek's Green MedTech 50.

These affirm mid-teens organic growth through 2026, shaping trends in 7 million joint replacements and 1.5 million AFib cases, lowering care costs 20% per our NEJM Mako study.

Now, let's talk about organic revenue growth by segment and geography. Excluding NeuroStim Dynamics acquisition and FX, we achieved 9.2% organic growth, accelerating from Q1's 7.8% and topping our 8-9% guide. This stems from structural heart and endoscopy volumes, stable pricing, and adjacencies like neuromodulation and digital therapeutics.

By segment: Cardiovascular, 45% of revenue, led at 12.5%, with structural heart at 15% on 22% VitalFlow TAVR unit growth to 14% U.S. share, narrowing on Edwards' Sapien and Medtronic's Evolut; U.S. TAVR volumes up 18% per DAR 360, rhythm management ICDs/pacemakers 9% via VitalPredict AI boosting success 12%. Offset by 2% ASP erosion, countered by bioresorbable stents.

Endoscopy & Surgical, 28%, grew 8.7%; VisioClear single-use duodenoscopes up 11% post-recall scrutiny like Boston Scientific/Olympus, GI volumes +14% per SGNA, VizRobotics efficiency +20%; general surgery 5% softer from flu delays, but harmonic scalpels in bariatrics riding GLP-1 wave.

Orthopedics & Spine, 17%, 6.8% amid high-single-digit ASP declines from GPO talks; hip/knee 9% on 12% Cementless Trinity volumes vs. Stryker Mako/Zimmer ROSA; spine neuromodulation 14% post-VitalSpine FDA for $3B SCS market at 12% CAGR, 15-20% better fixation.

Diabetes & Diagnostics, 10%, soared 16.2%; VitalSense CGM +25%, 2.1 million monthly users +30% via OTC and Apple Health like Dexcom G7; diagnostics 8% with VitalScan PSA +18% specificity.

By geography, constant currency: U.S. 62% at 10.4%, up from 9.1%, via CMS 2024 PFS, 1,200 reps +2ppt share, DTC diabetes with Teladoc. EMEA 22% at 7.9%, MDR delays hit €50M endoscopy but ex-UK 9%, TAVR +16% per EFPIA. APAC 12% at 11.2%, China 14% post-reopen +200bps, Shanghai-Mindray VitalFlow NMPA, Japan 8% robotic spine, India 25% ortho. Rest of World 4% at 5.6%, LATAM +12%.

Under VitalCore 3.0, 60% R&D to digital AI/remote monitoring contributes 15% incremental growth; 1.5ppt YTD share per IQVIA. Q3 outlook 9-11%, upside TAVR expansions, GLP-1 bariatrics; $2.5B cash for 10%+ M&A.

Moving on to procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary. Procedure volumes grew 18% globally year-over-year, accelerating from Q2's 14%, fifth straight double-digit quarter, outpacing medtech's 12% per IQVIA/Procedure Intelligence.

Structural heart led: EvoClip TMVR/TAVR +28% global, U.S. 32% on CMS NCD, CLASP IID data, 22% TMVR share via streamlined delivery/less fluoroscopy.

Peripheral +22%, Tack System +45% for CLI vs. BD Lutonix post-DETOUR2. Endoscopy +15%, single-use duodenoscopes in ASCs post-scandals. Orthopedics +16%, robotics +25% for outpatient MACRA shifts.

U.S. 55% revenue +21%, backlogs cleared 95% pre-COVID, ASCs +35%. Europe 12%, MDR navigated with 85% Class III renewals, Germany/France 98% 2019 levels, IN.PACT DCB gains. APAC +26%, China +40% MicroPort TAVR vs. Edwards, India endoscopy +30%.

Three pillars: $250M R&D for AI 3D TEE/pulsed-field ablation vs. Medtronic Thermocool; 1,200 reps +40% ASC coverage; dual-source 99% delivery. Tailwinds: 5M annual TAVR-eligible by 2025, ortho robotics to 30%, IPPS pass-throughs. Q4 16-19%, full-year 17% for 12-14% revenue growth.

Next, capital equipment versus consumables mix trends. This drives our predictable recurring model: capital like Precision Robotics and Horizon Imaging (50-60% margins), consumables like single-use instruments/catheters (75-80%).

Consumables hit 72% mix, up from 68% year-ago/70% Q2 sequential, sixth straight expansion; $922M +22% on 12% volumes/3pt ASP from FlexiCath. Capital 22% at $282M +4%, services 6%. Five-year shift from 55% FY2019 adds $450M recurring, like Intuitive's 75%+ or Stryker endoscopy.

Drivers: 4,200 Precision Robotics +18%, 2,800 Horizon +11%; utilization 85%/78%, attach 1.25 kits + from 1.18, BioShield -22% infections. Precision 3.0 upgrade ($250K capital/$50K SaaS) +15% pull-through; Horizon AI +9% kits.

Regions: U.S. 52% revenue 75% consumables +5pts, IDN bundles; Europe 28% 70% +20% NHS wins; APAC 15% 68% +6pts China Mindray FlexiCath, base doubled; ROW 5% Brazil ASCs +25%.

Consumables 85% gross profit at 78% margin; target 75% FY2025 via 15-20% base growth, $400M capital, $180M EndoVance tuck-in +$50M disposables, mid-single ASP. Q4 consumables 20-23%, capital 5-8%; 92% OTR mitigates risks for mid-teens EPS.

Finally, R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress. Innovation fuels growth, TAM expansion, clinical outcomes in value-based/personalized medicine.

Q3 R&D $452 million, 11.2% sales up from 10.8%, +14% year-over-year outpacing 9% revenue; full-year $1.8B +12% from 2022, vs. Medtronic/Boston Scientific/Abbott, EU MDR/FDA TPLC.

Allocation: cardiovascular 38% +3pts on structural heart demographics; orthopedics/spine 25%, neurostimulation 22%, digital/robotics 15%; TAM from $45B interventional cardiology/$30B neuromodulation.

28 programs +4 year-ago, 150+ staff in Minneapolis/Galway/Singapore: 5 late-stage, 12 mid, 11 preclinical.

Highlights: EvoValve Pro TAVR 6-month IDE data 250 patients—95% success, 1.2% mortality, <2% leak like Edwards Sapien; PMA Q1 2024, CE mid-year, $1.2B peak in $8B 15% CAGR TAVR.

LithoAI Ultra OCT AI imaging Breakthrough Designation; ML calcium/stent optimization -22% times, 98% accuracy 75 patients; U.S. pivotal enrolling final 400 for Q2 510(k), $2.5B coronary market post-OPTICO-PCI.

EvoStim HF first-in-human Australia +35% 6-min walk vs. sham like Boston MultiSense; IDE U.S. Q4, ICD combos.

Regions: U.S. 3 510(k)s; Europe 2 MDR DCB renewals vs. Concept Medical; APAC Shanghai 2 NMPA DES, MicroPort neurostim 2025 in $15B 18% China market/Healthy China 2030.

ROI: 22% Q3 revenue from <3-year launches, +5pt margins on pricing/LoS; Galway 40% recycled prototyping EU Green Deal/Stryker-like.

Ahead: 4 launches 2024-2025 +300-400bps growth; $2.5B cash, 4% CAPEX vs. delays/reimbursement risks.

Our R&D positions us to lead $500B industry demographics/digital.

I will now turn the call over to Lisa for a review of our financial results.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Michael. As Michael highlighted, we delivered strong financial performance this quarter. Net revenue of $1.28 billion grew 14% reported, 15% organically. Gross margin expanded to 68.5%, up 180 basis points, driven by consumables mix and manufacturing efficiencies in our Galway and Shanghai facilities.

Operating expenses rose 12% to $415 million, reflecting R&D at 11.2% and SG&A investments in our sales force, but leverage improved operating margin to 28.4%. Adjusted EPS $1.62, up 17%. Balance sheet solid with $2.5 billion cash, debt-to-EBITDA 1.8x.

For Q4, we guide organic revenue growth of 10-12%, full-year 12-14%; adjusted EPS $1.65-$1.70. Mid-teens growth into 2025, supported by pipeline launches and share gains.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Raj Patel for an update on our product pipeline.

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. I'm excited to share updates on our innovative pipeline. We recently received FDA clearance for LithoAI Ultra, a groundbreaking AI-enabled intravascular imaging system that integrates real-time machine learning for automated calcium detection and stent optimization, reducing procedure times significantly.

Building on the milestones Michael covered, our EvoValve Pro TAVR is on track for PMA submission, with stellar safety data. EvoStim HF advances to U.S. trials, and we're progressing 28 programs overall, with emphasis on AI, robotics, and neuromodulation to expand TAM and outcomes.

Now, back to Michael for Q&A.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Raj. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star then one. Our first question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee - JPMorgan:
Thanks, good morning. Great results. Can you expand on the organic growth outlook for Q4 and into next year, especially with potential ASP pressures?

Michael Reynolds:
Thanks, David. We're confident in 10-12% Q4 organic growth, full-year 12-14%, accelerating next year to mid-teens. Procedure tailwinds, TAVR expansions, and GLP-1 adjacencies offset ASP from GPOs; pricing discipline holds mid-single digits via premium innovations like BioShield.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter - Goldman Sachs:
Thanks. On R&D, how do you view ROI from the pipeline amid competition and regulatory risks?

Lisa Chen:
Emily, solid question. Pipeline drove 22% Q3 revenue at +5pt margins; four 2024-2025 launches add 300-400bps growth. $1.8B spend well-capitalized by $2.5B cash; risks like delays mitigated by diversified hubs and partnerships. Peers' challenges like MDR give us edge with proactive renewals.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for that insight, Lisa.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mark Thompson with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mark Thompson - Barclays:
Congrats on the quarter. Tom, thoughts on market share gains in cardiovascular and endoscopy amid competitive bundling?

Tom Hargrove:
Mark, thanks. CV share +2ppt to 14% TAVR via 1,200 reps and ASC push; endoscopy 11% on VisioClear post-recalls, VizRobotics efficiency. Bundling countered by VitalCore focus on outcomes—22% TAVR volumes, GI +14%. Targeting 1.5ppt YTD per IQVIA.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for that insight, Tom.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Priya Singh with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Priya Singh - Morgan Stanley:
Good morning. Raj, update on EvoStim HF timeline and combo synergies?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Priya, EvoStim hit first-in-human with 35% walk test improvement; IDE approved, U.S. Q4 start. Synergies with ICDs via MultiSense-like sensing; peak potential in heart failure, de-risked by Australia data and regional JVs.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for your questions. Before we conclude, I want to thank our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support. We are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
